what: Photo Editor lets you improve a photo right in your browser: pick one of 15 filters, then fine-tune exposure, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, saturation, vibrance, warmth, tint, sharpening, vignette and film grain.

It also crops to common shapes, rotates, flips and straightens tilted horizons. The preview is screen-sized so sliders feel instant, while the download is processed at the full resolution of your photo in a background worker, so even 12 megapixel phone photos save in a second or two.
Your photo is never uploaded, and your original file is never changed.
uses: Fix dark or dull phone photos
Lift shadows, add a little exposure and vibrance to rescue a photo taken in poor light.
Give a set of photos one look
Apply the same filter, such as Golden Hour or Matte, to make holiday or product photos feel consistent.
Crop to 1:1, 4:5 or 9:16 so the important part fills an Instagram post or a story.
Use the straighten slider to level a tilted sea or skyline; the edges are trimmed so no blank corners appear.
Try Noir for drama or Silver for a soft classic look.
Brighten, sharpen a little and crop square for an online shop.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a photo here" or drag a JPG, PNG or WebP file onto it. The photo appears with a row of filter thumbnails made from your own picture.
Click a filter such as Vivid, Warm or Noir. Use "Filter strength" to make it subtler. Click Original to remove it.

Move the sliders under "Adjust". Exposure and Brightness lighten the photo, Highlights and Shadows recover bright and dark areas, Warmth and Tint change the colour cast, and Saturation and Vibrance change how colourful it is. Double-click a slider to reset it.
Sharpen brings out detail, Vignette darkens (or lightens, if negative) the corners, and Grain adds a film-like texture.
Click "Crop and rotate". Choose a crop shape, drag the box or its corners, rotate or flip, and use Straighten to level the picture. Click Done.
Press and hold "Hold to compare" to see the original. Use Undo and Redo (or Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y) to step through your changes.
Choose JPG, PNG or WebP and the quality, then click "Download full size". The file is named like photo-edited.jpg.
features: Vivid, Warm, Cool, Golden Hour, Faded, Noir, Silver, Sepia, Teal & Orange, Pastel, Moody, Retro, Crisp, Matte and Lush, each with a strength slider.
Exposure, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, saturation, vibrance, warmth, tint, sharpen, vignette and grain.
Crop to free, original, square, 4:5, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9 or 9:16, turn in quarter steps, mirror, and level up to 45 degrees.
See the original at any moment without losing your edits.
Up to 60 steps, with keyboard shortcuts.
Processed in a background worker so large photos do not freeze the page. JPG, PNG or WebP with adjustable quality.
Nothing is uploaded and camera details such as location are not copied into the saved file.

example.title: Worked example: a dull beach photo for Instagram
example.text: Sara has a 4000 × 3000 px beach photo that looks grey and slightly tilted. She clicks Golden Hour and sets its strength to 70%, then raises Shadows to 25 and Vibrance to 20. In Crop and rotate she picks Portrait 4:5, sets Straighten to -2° so the sea is level, drags the box over herself and clicks Done. The info line shows Full size: 2385 × 2981 px. She holds Compare to check the difference, chooses JPG at 92% and downloads beach-edited.jpg.

tips: Small moves look most natural: try values between 10 and 30 before going further.
Vibrance boosts dull colours more than strong ones, so it keeps skin tones natural better than Saturation.
Raise Shadows and lower Highlights to bring back detail in bright skies and dark areas.
Sharpen is applied per pixel, so judge it zoomed in on the downloaded file; 20 to 40 suits most photos.
Use PNG only when you need a lossless file; JPG at 85 to 92% is much smaller and looks the same.
Keep your original photo. The tool always saves a new copy.
problems: The browser cannot read that format, such as HEIC from an iPhone or a camera RAW file. Convert it to JPG first, or change your phone camera setting to Most Compatible.
Click the green Download button that appears under Download full size. Some browsers block automatic downloads.
The saved photo is smaller than the original
You cropped it. The info line under the preview shows the exact size that will be saved.
The page says the photo is too large
Photos over about 50 megapixels can exceed your browser's memory. Resize the photo first, then edit it.
Some older browsers, like older Safari, cannot save WebP. Choose JPG instead.
